# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

screens.why3: Every super knows how long last night's log took them, so this is pure recall of their own evening.
screens.why4: The time rungs are mostly distinct, but 'a couple of hours after the walk' and 'the rest of the evening' can be the same night for a super who leaves the trailer at six, so they overlap a bit.
screens.why5: These are my rungs and my measure, hours spent getting the log done, with nothing about videos, texting the crew or Fresco leaking in.
screens.why7: One measure (time spent typing up, ending in never done that day), five rungs best to worst, the first a working rung, the line under it, so the belief can go either way; the escape belongs on the stranger's item, not this Check.
screens.instead: Keep it, but make rung 4 a time step that can't overlap rung 3: 'Took three hours or more, into the evening'.

screens.why1: Right after I said how supes do the log today, it makes sense to check the rungs of how that log-writing went before Keel tests whether it falls short.
screens.why2: 'The walk', 'the trailer', 'typed up', 'written up that day' are exactly how a super talks about the daily log, readable on first pass.
screens.why3: Every super knows how long last night's log took them and whether it got done, so the answer comes from their own day.
screens.why4: 'Took about an hour in the trailer' and 'Took about an hour to type up' mean the same thing, so a super who spent an hour in the trailer has two true answers, while the 2-to-3-hour evening I actually pitch has no rung of its own between an hour and 'the rest of the evening'.
screens.why5: The time measure is mine, but my headline number, 'up to 3 hours a day' and 'a few hours', has no rung of its own, and the rewrite left a duplicate where that step should be.
screens.why7: The rungs are on one measure (time to write up), five long, working rung first, failing outright last, line under a working rung with both sides possible, but rungs 2 and 3 are not distinct steps on that measure, which bends the card's 'each rung a distinct step' rule.
screens.instead: Typed up within half an hour of the walk · Took about an hour · Took two to three hours · Took the rest of the evening · Never got written up that day

screens.why1: Choosing who asks the questions is the right step just before the study goes out to supers, and nothing earlier asked it.
screens.why2: A founder reads this in one pass: two named voices, a play button each, the cost in credits, and the note that people get a text link either way.
screens.why3: It is my own call about my own study, and I can hear both voices before I pick.
screens.why4: Two distinct voices, each with a 5-second preview and a clear default; no escape is needed for a pick like this.
screens.why5: It says the voice asks construction superintendents, but my Part 3 also goes to the contractor's operations leads who pay, and the screen leaves them out.
screens.instead: Who should ask your questions to construction superintendents and the contractors' operations leads? (Daphne ▶ / Saskia ▶)

screens.why1: Once I've picked who asks, choosing how my supers answer the link is the obvious next step before it goes out.
screens.why2: Plain words: talking, typing, tapping, a link to open -- nothing I'd need to read twice.
screens.why3: I know my supers -- in the truck or the trailer, phone in hand, often with gloves and noise -- so I can pick the format they'll actually finish.
screens.why4: Three distinct, complete choices (AI video, read-and-tap, let them pick) with no overlap and nothing missing for this decision.
screens.why5: It's about the study's delivery, not my product, so nothing of Fresco or the buyer roles leaks and my pick of Read and tap stands as typed.

screens.why1: After choosing how superintendents answer, deciding who gets the link is the obvious last step before sending.
screens.why2: Each option is plain and says what happens next; 'Contacts page' is Keel's own term but explained in place.
screens.why3: I know whether I'm texting supers I've met on site walks in Napa and the South Bay or posting a link somewhere, so I can answer from my own situation.
screens.why4: The three options are distinct and cover the cases, but the middle option reads like a manual ('Pick a list; Keel makes a link for each one, and you send them') rather than in my words, and it is unclear whether I can mix supers I know with a found list.
screens.why5: My pick, the supers I know by name each getting their own link, is kept as I chose it, and nothing of Fresco's product leaks to a respondent here.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? — Supers I know by name (each gets their own link) / People from a Keel contact search (each gets their own link) / One open link I post where supers already are

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" sits right under the title with "Frequency: 4 counted" beside it, and the card spells out that 5 were needed, so I know the stage is undecided and why; it does name only Frequency when Importance and Current solution are short too.
screens.why_b2: The tally and the Prevalence line (6 of 7, bar 6 of 7) read at once, but "4 to 7 counted" and "4 counted" don't say why three of my seven supers dropped out, so I need a second look to see whom each card is over.
screens.why_b3: The dimension names and the statement are mine, but the Importance line ("have five things that are hard... one of the two") and "still falls short" are Keel's phrasing of my belief that supers burn hours in the trailer, so they are recognisable rather than my words.
screens.why_b4: Nothing tells me what to do: no line saying one more counted answer would decide Frequency, Importance and Current solution, or whom to send the study to next; "What it measures" only explains the rule.
screens.why_b5: n=7 is in the kicker, three cards say plainly they are too few, and Prevalence is shown as exactly at the bar (6 of 7) rather than called strong, so nothing is claimed beyond the seven who answered.
screens.instead: Too few to call: only 4 of 7 supers could be counted on how often, how much it hurts and how they cope today (3 dropped because ...), and 5 are needed; get one or two more superintendents to answer before reading the problem as held or not.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Holding up' sits right beside '6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar', so I see both the verdict and the number that decides it.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows 6 for and 1 against over 7 people, with my bar marked at 6, though the label 'your bar · 6 of 7 (at least 8 in 10) 0 7' is cramped.
screens.why_b3: Prevalence and 'At least 8 in 10' are mine, but the belief now reads 'typed site notes into the daily log' and drops 'on commercial jobs' and 'after the site walks', which was the costly part I meant.
screens.why_b4: The So line only says how often and whether it matters are on the next two cards, which tells me nothing about what passing exactly at the bar means for Fresco.
screens.why_b5: It keeps n=7 visible, calls it 'a small group: a lean, not a call', and says 'at your bar exactly' instead of claiming strength.
screens.instead: Holding up, just: 6 of the 7 supers typed the day's notes into the log after their walks, exactly my 8-in-10 bar, and one more No would have sunk it. Seven is a lean, so check Frequency and Importance before leaning on it.

screens.why_b1: The verdict Too few to call sits right beside its deciding number, 4 counted and 5 needed, so I know why there is no call yet.
screens.why_b2: I can see four people at 5 days and the middle answer, but the 0 tick suggests a button nobody had, and your bar 4 of 5 (at least 2 in 3) next to a marker at 4 takes a second look to tell from my own 4-to-5 range.
screens.why_b3: Frequency and 4 to 5 working days out of 5 are mine, but type site notes into the daily log is narrower than my getting the walk's photos and notes into the log, and the Asked line's the most recent time it happened does not fit a count question.
screens.why_b4: Nothing is settled here yet is generic; it does not tell me that one more counted superintendent decides it, or that all four counted so far were inside my range.
screens.why_b5: The small group is called a lean, not a call, which is honest, but a bar reading 4 of 5 beside four supporting answers could be taken as already met, and Hank's would rather not say is printed twice.
screens.instead: Four of four counted superintendents logged notes on 4 or 5 of the last 5 working days, with a middle answer of 5; one more counted answer is needed to call it, so send the study to a few more supers.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its number, 4 counted with 5 needed to call it, so I know where I stand and why.
screens.why_b2: The bars count picks (8) but the strip counts people (4), and 'your bar · 4 of 5' next to '4 counted' took me a second look to realise it means 4 of 5 must pick it, not that 4 of 5 did.
screens.why_b3: The card is Importance, and the belief is my end-of-day log problem in my terms, typing the site notes into the daily log once the walks are done, with the schedule, subs, RFIs and safety follow-ups beside it.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say it's 2 for and 2 against, that both against put schedule and subs first, or that one more answer cannot reach 4 of 5, so I'd need several more supers before this could hold.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, the two not counted are named with why, and the small group is called out, so nothing claims more than the 4 can carry.
screens.instead: 2 of 4 put the log in their two; Denise and Ray put the schedule and subs first. Even a fifth 'for' leaves you at 3 of 5, under your bar of 4, so ask more supers whether the log or the schedule eats their evening.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, 4 counted with 5 needed, and the So line repeats both, so I know where this stands and why.
screens.why_b2: The rungs, the counts and the line read quickly, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' with only 4 counted and a ghost cell made me stop to work out that the bar assumes a fifth person, and the two near-identical 'about an hour' rungs needed a second look.
screens.why_b3: Current solution and the daily log after the site walk are my job in my words, but 'Typed up within half an hour of the walk' is Keel's rewritten rung rather than my own, and the flow recorded no belief line I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't tell me that one more counted super decides it, or that 3 of 4 already lean toward the log costing an hour or more.
screens.why_b5: No claim goes beyond the six who answered: n stays visible, the uncounted (Hank and Luis) are named with reasons, and the small group is called a lean, not a call.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 counted supers took an hour or more to type up the log after the walk, a lean toward falling short; one more counted answer decides it, and 'about an hour in the trailer' and 'about an hour to type up' should be one rung.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' and '4 counted · 5 needed' sit together, but the screen never says which way the 4 lean (how many for, how many against), so I can't tell whether the 2 against are half or most of what counted.
screens.why_b3: Importance and the belief line — typing site notes into the daily log as one of the two they'd most like made easier — are the words I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: Nothing says what to do next: no 'reach one more superintendent', no line on what the schedule-and-subs pull means for pitching Fresco as a log tool.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible, low n is said outright as too few to call, and the theme is shown as 2 voices, not a trend.
screens.why_b6: Denise finishing on the tablet before the gate and Ray's 'the log can wait till morning, the deck can't' tell me the competing pain is tomorrow's schedule and subs — a pitch angle (log as a by-product of the walk that feeds the schedule) I hadn't written.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 2 of 4 put the log outside their top two, both for tomorrow's schedule and subs — reach one more super, and test whether Fresco's walk notes can feed the schedule, not just the log.

screens.why1: As the first screen it makes sense to check whether my jobs are on Procore or ACC before asking anything about my daily logs.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are the platforms every super I know works in, and 'jobs you are running now' is how I'd say it myself.
screens.why3: I know without guessing which platform each of my jobs is on.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it completely, and a gate question needs no escape.
screens.why5: It names the platforms my jobs run on and gives away nothing about whatever they're building.
screens.why6: It's short and easy to hear, and 'ACC' is spoken as three letters every super knows, though for a gate 'Yes or no' alone would be tighter than 'I'll read two options'.

screens.why1: Right after confirming I'm on Procore or ACC, asking whether I did the daily log this week is the obvious next step before getting into a story.
screens.why2: Typing site notes into the daily log is exactly how I'd say it, nothing to read twice.
screens.why3: I do the daily log every working day, so I know straight off whether I did it in the last five.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it cleanly, and the two chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to this gate.
screens.why5: Nothing about the product leaks to me, but the gate drops the 'after your site walks' part, so it no longer asks about the after-the-fact typing the founder counted, only the log itself.
screens.why6: One short question with 'Yes or no' on the end; easy to hear once and answer.
screens.why7: Every super on a Procore job types notes into the daily log every week, so this asks the routine, not the problem; nobody truly says No and the founder's band can never be refuted.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you type up the daily log after your site walks? Yes · No

screens.why1: Right after I said yes to typing notes into the daily log this week, asking on how many of those days I did it is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Working days, site notes, daily log: that's exactly how I talk about it, and I can answer on first read.
screens.why3: I know which days I sat down and typed up the log this week, so I can count it straight off.
screens.why4: One button for each day from 1 to 5 covers every true answer for somebody who already said yes, and 'I can't recall' fits as the way out.
screens.why5: Nothing about anybody's product or plan comes through; it's just my log and my week.
screens.why6: It's short and it's one question, and 'a number from 1 to 5, or say you can't recall' is easy to hold when I hear it.
screens.why7: It counts days of the window, said once in the window phrase, with buttons 1 to 5, no zero, the escape apart, and an act I either did or didn't do on a given day; whether it can count against depends on the founder's low being 2 or more, which this screen doesn't show.

screens.why1: Right after asking how often I type notes into the log, it makes sense to ask whether that is the part of the walk aftermath I'd most want off my plate.
screens.why2: RFIs, subs, schedule, safety issues and daily log are all my own words, though I'd say 'your last day on site' rather than 'day of site walks' since I walk every day.
screens.why3: Every row is something I do myself at the end of the day after the walk, so I can answer from what I actually did.
screens.why4: The rows are distinct and the escape fits, but the log row says only notes, and for me the real drag is the photos, the hours spent uploading and tagging them into Procore.
screens.why5: Nothing leaks, but the founder's problem was getting the photos and notes into the log, and this narrows it to typing notes, dropping the photo half where the hours go.
screens.why6: It is one short question with five short parallel options and one escape, easy to hold on a single hearing.
screens.why7: The measure, the count, the own row not first, the four rivals and None of these at the first ask are all met, but the own row splits the photos-and-notes pair into one part, which bends the rule to keep both halves of a pair.
screens.instead: Think of your last day on site. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Writing up RFIs for issues found on the walk; updating the schedule after the walk; lining up subs for tomorrow; following up on safety issues from the walk; or getting the day's photos and notes into the daily log. Or say none of these.

screens.why1: After asking how often I typed site notes in and which part I'd want easier, asking how the last daily log went is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Daily log, site walk and trailer are my everyday words, and I get the question on first read even though it says 'daily log' twice.
screens.why3: I write the log up every day, so I know how long my last one took.
screens.why4: 'Took about an hour in the trailer' and 'Took about an hour to type up' are the same answer, and if mine took two hours there is no option for it short of 'the rest of the evening'.
screens.why5: It is about typing up my log after the walk, and nothing about anybody's product or plan reaches me.
screens.why6: Heard aloud, two 'about an hour' options in a row make me stop and ask what the difference is, which breaks holding the list.
screens.why7: Every rung is on time, the first is the log done fine and the last is never done, and the escape is there, but rungs 2 and 3 are the same step on the scale, with a place added to one, so the five are not five distinct steps.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. How long did it take to type up after the walk? Done within half an hour; about an hour; two or three hours; took the rest of the evening; or never got written up that day. Or say someone else did it.
